extracted.intended_audience: students of algebraic geometry (Math 216); advanced undergraduates and graduate students learning foundations of algebraic geometry
extracted.subtask_description: Exposition and exercises developing foundational constructions and theorems in algebraic geometry: Hilbert and Grassmannian parameter spaces, hypersurface parameter spaces, completion/power-series techniques, singularity definitions, the Theorem on Formal Functions, Zariski connectedness and Stein factorization, and resolution of curve singularities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hilbert functor (Hilb_B P^n) definition
rubrics_metrics.description: Hilb_B P^n is the contravariant functor sending a scheme B to finitely presented closed subschemes of P^n_B that are flat over B (with pullbacks giving the functoriality).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasizes finite presentation and flatness over the base B; think of Hilb as parametrizing flat families of closed subschemes of projective space. (Used as the basic object whose representability is asserted in the Hilbert scheme theorem.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Representability of the Hilbert functor (Theorem 28.3.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: Hilb_Z P^n is representable by a scheme locally of finite type (Grothendieck).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: References given for construction; this is the foundational representability result from which base-change yields Hilb_B P^n representability (see Easy Exercise 28.3.A).

rubrics_metrics.name: Base-change/universal property for Hilbert scheme
rubrics_metrics.description: Given representability for B = Z (the universal case), Hilb_B P^n is represented by Hilb_Z P^n ×_Z B, so the general case follows from the universal case.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Shows how representability for the universal base produces representability over arbitrary B by pullback/base-change.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hilbert polynomial stratification
rubrics_metrics.description: Hilb_Z P^n decomposes as the disjoint union over Hilbert polynomials p(m) of subschemes whose fibers have fixed Hilbert polynomial p(m).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each connected component corresponds to a fixed Hilbert polynomial; use Corollary 24.7.3 as hinted in the exercises.

rubrics_metrics.name: Projectivity of Hilbert scheme (Theorem 28.3.2)
rubrics_metrics.description: Each Hilb_Z^{p(m)} P^n (the component for a fixed Hilbert polynomial p(m)) is projective over Z.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Gives a stronger representability statement: the representing scheme is projective, not merely locally finite type.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grassmannian as parameter space for linear P^{k-1}-families
rubrics_metrics.description: The functor G'(k,n) assigning to B the set of finitely presented closed subschemes X ⊂ P^{n-1}_B, flat over B, whose fibers are P^{k-1}, is represented by the Grassmannian G(k,n).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Construction uses Proj and the Sym• construction: a locally free rank k quotient Q of O_B^n gives Proj_B Sym• Q → P^{n-1}_B with fibers P^{k-1}; conversely, use cohomology and base change to recover Q from a family of embedded P^{k-1}'s (Exercises 28.3.C–E).

rubrics_metrics.name: Cohomology-and-base-change criteria for Grassmannian construction
rubrics_metrics.description: For a family X ⊂ P^{n-1}_B with fibers P^{k-1}, Riπ_* O_X(1) = 0 for i>0 and π_* O_X(1) is locally free of rank k; the pushforward long exact sequence yields a short exact sequence 0 → π_* I_X(1) → π_* O_{P^{n-1}_B}(1) → π_* O_X(1) → 0 with ranks n−k, n, k respectively.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These vanishing and locally-freeness statements are obtained by Cohomology and Base Change (Theorem 28.1.6) and identify π_* O_X(1) as the desired locally free quotient giving the map to G(k,n).

rubrics_metrics.name: Inverse constructions identify functor and Grassmannian
rubrics_metrics.description: The two constructions — from quotient sheaves to embedded P^{k-1}-families via Proj Sym•, and from embedded P^{k-1}-families to quotient sheaves via π_* O_X(1) — are inverses, establishing that G(k,n) represents G'(k,n).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exercises direct to 'close the loop' showing the bijection/natural equivalence of the two constructions; this is the method of proof for representability of the Grassmannian.

rubrics_metrics.name: Functor of degree-d hypersurfaces (H_{d,n})
rubrics_metrics.description: H_{d,n} assigns to a scheme B closed subschemes X ⊂ P^n_B, flat and finitely presented over B, whose fibers are degree d hypersurfaces in P^n; pullback gives functoriality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This functor is used to show representability of the family of degree-d hypersurfaces by projective space of appropriate dimension.

rubrics_metrics.name: Representation of hypersurface functor (Proposition 28.3.6)
rubrics_metrics.description: The functor H_{d,n} is represented by P^{(n+d choose d) - 1}.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The proof mirrors the Grassmannian argument: use the exact sequence twisted by O(d), show higher pushforwards vanish, and identify π_* I_X(d) as a rank-1 locally free subsheaf of a free sheaf of rank N = (n+d choose d), then dualize to get the map to projective space; close the loop as in Exercise 28.3.H.

rubrics_metrics.name: Completion (I-adic) definition and notation
rubrics_metrics.description: For a ring A and a decreasing sequence of ideals J_n (often J_n = I^n), the completion is the limit lim_{←} A/J_n, denoted ^A; for I-adic completion write Â (completion of A along I).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Completion is given a topology (inverse limit topology) and is fundamental for formal/local arguments; the important special case is completion at a maximal ideal giving formal power series rings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Noetherian completion properties (Theorem 29.2.6)
rubrics_metrics.description: If A is Noetherian and I ⊂ A an ideal, then (a) ^A is flat over A; (b) for finitely generated A-modules M, the natural map ^A ⊗_A M → ^M is an isomorphism; (c) completion preserves exact sequences of finitely generated modules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof proceeds by reducing to the exactness statement (c) and uses Artin–Rees; caution: completion need not be exact for arbitrary (non-finitely-generated) modules — an explicit counterexample is given.

rubrics_metrics.name: Power-series/completion examples and Cohen structure remarks
rubrics_metrics.description: k[[x_1,...,x_n]] is the completion of k[x_1,...,x_n] at the maximal ideal (x_1,...,x_n); for a Noetherian local k-algebra (A,m,k) of dimension d with chosen generators lifting a basis of m/m^2, there is a surjection k[[t_1,...,t_n]] → ^A (Exercise 29.2.C) — a special case of Cohen Structure Theorem.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This motivates interpreting elements of completed local rings as formal power series expansions; completion often makes regular schemes look like affine space formally.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of node via completion (29.3.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: A scheme X has a node at a closed point p if the completion of O_{X,p} at its maximal ideal is isomorphic (as topological rings) to k[[x,y]]/(xy).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This formal-local definition gives the algebraic notion of a node; exercises characterize nodes for plane curve equations and discuss split vs non-split nodes over non-algebraically-closed fields.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definitions of cusp, tacnode, triple point, ordinary m-fold point (29.3.3)
rubrics_metrics.description: Over an algebraically closed field (char ≠ 2,3), X has a cusp, tacnode, triple point if ^O_{X,p} is isomorphic to the completion of k[x,y]/(y^2 - x^3), k[x,y]/(y^2 - x^4), k[x,y]/(y^3 - x^3) respectively; ordinary m-fold point means completion is that of k[x,y]/(f) with f homogeneous degree m with no repeated roots.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These singularity types are defined formally-locally by specifying a formal model; exercises connect these definitions to geometric invariants like the δ-invariant and genus contributions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Theorem on Formal Functions (29.4.2)
rubrics_metrics.description: For a proper morphism π: X → Y of locally Noetherian schemes and a coherent sheaf F on X, the natural map (completion of Riπ_* F at q) → lim_{←} H^i(X_n, F|_{X_n}) is an isomorphism for all i, where X_n is the n-th infinitesimal neighborhood (thickening) of the fiber over q.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interpretation: the completed stalk of the higher direct images equals the limit of cohomology on infinitesimal thickenings of the fiber; warning: the theorem does not assert anything about the finite-level base-change maps themselves (the individual maps to H^i(X_n,·)). The proof is technical and deferred.

rubrics_metrics.name: Zariski's Connectedness Lemma (29.5.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: If a proper morphism π: X → Y of locally Noetherian schemes is O-connected (π_* O_X = O_Y), then for every q ∈ Y the fiber π^{-1}(q) is connected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof uses formal neighborhoods and idempotent-trick: disconnectedness would give nontrivial idempotents in the completed local ring ^O_{Y,q}, contradicting that ^O_{Y,q} is local; relies on completion preserving the needed properties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stein factorization (29.5.3)
rubrics_metrics.description: Any proper morphism π: X → Y of locally Noetherian schemes factors canonically as X --α→ Y' --β→ Y where β is finite and α is O-connected, with Y' = Spec π_* O_X (so β is induced by the structure morphism).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Construction uses coherence of π_* O_X (Grothendieck's coherence theorem); consequences: α has connected fibers (Zariski connectedness), and the factorization is compatible with projectivity and base-change (exercises discuss flat base-change compatibility).

rubrics_metrics.name: Resolution-by-blowing-up strategy for projective curves
rubrics_metrics.description: To desingularize a reduced projective curve C over a field, iteratively blow up singular points; the arithmetic genus pa(C) is an integer invariant that (i) pa(C)=pa(Ĉ) iff C is already nonsingular (so normalization is iso), (ii) finite morphisms increase pa, and (iii) blowing up a singular point decreases pa, so the algorithm terminates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Arguments use the exact sequence 0 → O_C → π_* O_{C'} → G → 0 with G supported on finitely many points; χ computations give genus relations; Exercises 29.5.E and surrounding text guide verification that blowing up reduces pa and hence resolves singularities for curves.

rubrics_metrics.name: Base-change and formal neighborhood computations
rubrics_metrics.description: Computations of cohomology on formal neighborhoods may be done either by restricting/tensoring to the stalk O_{Y,q} or in any affine neighborhood of q; the completion of Riπ_* F at q is canonically the completion of Hi(X_B, F|_{X_B}) at the maximal ideal m_q when Spec B is an affine neighborhood of q.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This technical account clarifies how the limits in the Theorem on Formal Functions are formed in practice and how base-change maps induce compatible maps to cohomology of thickenings (29.4.1.1–1.2).
